title: tcspecial physics model
description: The vehicle's physical components, which tcssim's stand-ins measure and act on, and how they are joined: a file of its own, named by each simulator file that uses it, because a vehicle's physics outlives any one configuration of its payloads. Each element is a part simulated alone, with fixed terminals of its type's; a connection joins an output to an input of the same kind. A stand-in joins a terminal in the simulator file, with connects: element.terminal. Every figure is written with its unit. YAML only.

physics.description: The components, grouped by type: each entry is one key, `type` and the type, whose value is the list of that type's components, each named by its first key, `component: <name>`. The type decides a component's terminals and what else it states.

connections.description: How the components are joined, each from an output to an input of the same kind. An input that takes one output may be given one; a zone's heat takes the sum of every heater's.

from.description: An output, as the component's name and the terminal's joined by a dot: `heater_1.heat`.

to.description: An input, written as from is: `zone.heat`.

heater.description: A heater: a resistance on a supply, switched on and off. Its terminals are on, an input driven by a decision; heat, in W; and current, in A. Its on must be joined to a stand-in the vehicle drives.

component.description: What it is called, which a connection or a stand-in names it by: not empty, and with no dot in it.

power.description: What it gives out while on at its nominal voltage, written with its unit: `60 W`.

voltage.description: Its supply's nominal voltage, written with its unit: `28 V`. With its power, says what current it draws.

ripple.description: How far its supply's voltage wanders, as a fraction of nominal: the standard deviation, written bare. Its power goes as the square of its voltage and its current as the voltage.

ripple_time.description: How slowly its supply wanders, as a length of time. Required with `ripple` and refused without it.

thermal_zone.description: A thermal zone: one body at one temperature, which cools towards its environment and is warmed by the heat joined to it. Its terminals are heat, in W, the sum of every heater's joined to it; and temperature, in K.

component.description: What it is called, which a connection or a stand-in names it by: not empty, and with no dot in it.

environment.description: The temperature around it, written with its unit: `283.15 K`. A zone starts here unless `start` says otherwise, because a vehicle coming up cold is the case a thermostat exists for.

time_constant.description: How fast it loses the difference between itself and its environment, as a length of time: after one of these it has lost all but 1/e of it.

capacity.description: How much heat it takes to warm it a kelvin, written with its unit: `20 J/K`. What turns a heater's watts into kelvin a second.

swing.description: How far the environment swings either side of `environment`, written with its unit, as a sine wave: a day and a night, or an orbit's sun and shadow.

period.description: How long one swing takes, as a length of time. Required with `swing` and refused without it.

wander.description: How far the environment wanders at random, written with its unit: the standard deviation of a departure drawn back towards nought with `wander_time` as its time constant.

wander_time.description: How slowly the environment wanders, as a length of time. Required with `wander` and refused without it.

start.description: Where it starts, written with its unit: `292.15 K`. Left out, it starts at its environment.

sun.description: The sun: its terminal is light, a ratio, one in sunlight and nought in shadow. Each change is an event, foreseen from the orbit.

component.description: What it is called, which a connection or a stand-in names it by: not empty, and with no dot in it.

period.description: How long one orbit takes, as a length of time: `90 min`.

eclipse.description: How much of an orbit is in shadow, as a fraction, written bare: `0.35`. From nought up to but not one.

start.description: How far round the orbit it starts, from the start of its sunlight, as a fraction, written bare. Unstated is nought.

solar_array.description: A solar array: its terminals are light, an input taking a ratio, which must be joined; and current, in A, its full-sun current times the light.

component.description: What it is called, which a connection or a stand-in names it by: not empty, and with no dot in it.

current.description: What it gives in full sunlight, written with its unit: `7 A`.

load.description: A load: its terminals are shed, a decision, shedding it while asserted and never where nothing is joined; and current, in A, nought while shed.

component.description: What it is called, which a connection or a stand-in names it by: not empty, and with no dot in it.

current.description: What it draws while it is on, written with its unit: `2 A`.

bus.description: A power bus: its terminals are supply and demand, in A, each the sum of what is joined to it, and current, in A, supply less demand. It has no settings.

component.description: What it is called, which a connection or a stand-in names it by: not empty, and with no dot in it.

battery.description: A battery: its terminals are offered, in A, what the bus has left over, which must be joined; voltage, in V; current, in A, what flows in, nought into a full battery; and charge, a ratio. Reaching full or empty is an event, foreseen.

component.description: What it is called, which a connection or a stand-in names it by: not empty, and with no dot in it.

capacity.description: How much charge it holds full, written with its unit: `10 Ah`.

empty.description: Its open-circuit voltage empty, written with its unit: `24 V`.

full.description: Its open-circuit voltage full, more than empty: `33.2 V`.

resistance.description: Its internal resistance, written with its unit: `0.05 ohm`.

charge.description: How full it starts, as a fraction of its capacity, written bare: `0.6`.

engine.description: An engine: its terminals are throttle, an input taking a ratio, which must be joined; force, in N; and flow, the fuel it burns, in kg/s. Its fuel running out is an event, foreseen.

component.description: What it is called, which a connection or a stand-in names it by: not empty, and with no dot in it.

thrust.description: Its thrust at full throttle, written with its unit: `4500 N`.

isp.description: Its specific impulse, as a length of time: `311 s`.

fuel.description: The fuel it starts with, written with its unit: `100 kg`.

body.description: A body: its terminals are force, in N, and flow, in kg/s, each the sum of what is joined to it; altitude, in m; velocity, in m/s; and contact, a decision asserted on the ground. Reaching the ground is an event, found ahead of time.

component.description: What it is called, which a connection or a stand-in names it by: not empty, and with no dot in it.

mass.description: Its mass at the start, fuel and all, written with its unit: `1500 kg`.

gravity.description: The gravity it falls in, written with its unit: `1.62 m/s2`.

altitude.description: How high it starts, written with its unit: `500 m`. Not below nought.

velocity.description: How fast it starts, up more than nought, written with its unit: `-20 m/s`.
